answer.rationale: The mandate (18% cut) cannot be met by the incumbent, who has already refused to reopen price, and the contract lapses in 14 days with no auto-renew, so renew/negotiate/defer are effectively foreclosed this cycle. The low-cost vendor quote meets the mandate, supported by memory_c2's account of quick onboarding and accurate invoicing—but that memory reflects a single prior instance and doesn't speak to performance under a zero-buffer, 14-day cutover, which is exactly the condition we're in now (94% committed volume, no slack). Given the objective explicitly bars increasing delivery risk, I want to verify c2's original record before committing capital to a full switch, checking whether the source noted any lead-time or ramp-up caveats that consolidation may have smoothed over. I'm framing the action as a small guarded test/phased cutover rather than a full-volume switch, to hedge against the possibility that onboarding speed doesn't hold under current supply conditions—echoing the caution that made second-sourcing (c3) valuable during the prior shortage. This preserves the cost-mandate progress while limiting the blast radius if the new vendor underperforms on delivery.
